```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.3, dpi = 125)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
source("pld_validation.R", local = TRUE)
load("../../data/cod_obs.rda")

roots <- normalizePath(c(params$results, if (nzchar(params$extra_results)) params$extra_results),
  mustWork = TRUE)
read_runs <- function(pattern) {
  files <- unlist(lapply(roots, list.files, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE),
    use.names = FALSE)
  files <- files[!duplicated(basename(files), fromLast = TRUE)]
  setNames(lapply(files, readRDS), sub("[.]rds$", "", basename(files)))
}
inputs <- read_runs("^(controlled|sampling)-[0-9]+[.]rds$")
fits <- read_runs("^fit-(controlled|sampling)-[0-9]+-.*[.]rds$")
sampling_inputs <- inputs[startsWith(names(inputs), "sampling-")]
sampling <- lapply(Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$ok), sampling_inputs), "[[", "value")
n_controlled <- sum(vapply(inputs[startsWith(names(inputs), "controlled-")],
  function(x) isTRUE(x$ok), logical(1)))

arms <- c("Lognormal", "Survey PLD", "Catch PLD", "Both PLD",
  "Fixed detection", "No occurrence")
scenarios <- c(low = "Low", standard = "Standard", high = "High",
  exact = "Exact PLD", multinomial = "Variable age samples")
arm_palette <- c("#353535", "#126782", "#C44C27", "#258375", "#72529D", "#8C6F35")
names(arm_palette) <- arms
scenario_label <- function(x) factor(unname(scenarios[x]), levels = scenarios)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

fit_status <- bind_rows(data.frame(attempt = character(), design = character(),
  history = integer(), scenario = character(), resolution = integer(), model = character(),
  success = logical(), error = character(), warnings = integer()), lapply(names(fits), function(name) {
    record <- fits[[name]]
    keys <- strsplit(sub("^fit-", "", name), "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    data.frame(attempt = name, design = keys[1L], history = as.integer(keys[2L]),
      scenario = keys[3L], resolution = as.integer(sub("^a", "", keys[4L])),
      model = arms[as.integer(sub("^model", "", keys[5L]))],
      success = isTRUE(record$value$converged), error = record$error,
      warnings = length(record$warnings))
  }))
keys <- c("design", "scenario", "resolution", "history", "model")
fit_table <- function(name) {
  bind_rows(lapply(which(fit_status$success), function(i) {
    row <- fit_status[i, ]
    d <- fits[[row$attempt]]$value$metric[[name]]
    if (!is.null(d) && nrow(d)) cbind(row[keys], d, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}

annual <- fit_table("annual")
age_abundance <- fit_table("population_age")
pulse <- fit_table("pulse")
scale <- if (nrow(annual)) {
  annual |>
    filter(quantity == "ssb") |>
    group_by(across(all_of(keys))) |>
    summarise(ssb_ratio = median(est / truth), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scale_flag = !is.finite(ssb_ratio) | ssb_ratio < 0.1 | ssb_ratio > 10)
} else {
  mutate(fit_status[FALSE, keys], ssb_ratio = numeric(), scale_flag = logical())
}
planned_main <- 24L * 10L
attempted_main <- sum(fit_status$design == "sampling" & fit_status$resolution == 14L)
passed_main <- sum(fit_status$design == "sampling" & fit_status$resolution == 14L & fit_status$success)
failed_inputs <- sum(!vapply(sampling_inputs, function(x) isTRUE(x$ok), logical(1)))
study_complete <- length(sampling_inputs) == 24L &&
  attempted_main == length(sampling) * 10L

pulse_metrics <- if (nrow(pulse)) {
  bind_rows(
    transmute(pulse, across(all_of(keys)), metric = "M pulse height", est = height, truth = height_truth),
    transmute(pulse, across(all_of(keys)), metric = "Early F increase", est = F_height, truth = F_height_truth),
    transmute(pulse, across(all_of(keys)), metric = "Late F", est = F_late, truth = F_late_truth),
    transmute(pulse, across(all_of(keys)), metric = "Late M", est = M_late, truth = M_late_truth)
  ) |> mutate(signed = est - truth, absolute = abs(signed))
} else data.frame()
older <- if (nrow(age_abundance)) {
  d <- filter(age_abundance, resolution == 14L, year %in% 16:23, age %in% 10:14)
  tail <- filter(d, age == 14L) |> mutate(metric = "Ages 14+")
  before_tail <- filter(d, age %in% 10:13) |>
    group_by(across(all_of(c(keys, "year")))) |>
    filter(n_distinct(age) == 4L) |>
    summarise(est = sum(est), truth = sum(truth), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(metric = "Ages 10–13")
  bind_rows(tail, before_tail) |>
    filter(is.finite(est), est > 0, is.finite(truth), truth > 0) |>
    mutate(log_ratio = log(est / truth)) |>
    group_by(across(all_of(c(keys, "metric")))) |>
    summarise(signed = mean(log_ratio), absolute = mean(abs(log_ratio)), years = n(),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(years == length(16:23))
} else data.frame()

# Use the same history, monitoring data and age resolution for each comparison.
pair_models <- function(data, first, second, name) {
  if (!nrow(data)) return(data.frame())
  pair_keys <- c("design", "scenario", "resolution", "history", "metric")
  flagged <- left_join(data, select(scale, all_of(keys), scale_flag), by = keys)
  base <- filter(flagged, model == first) |>
    select(all_of(pair_keys), base = absolute, base_flag = scale_flag)
  filter(flagged, model == second) |>
    select(all_of(pair_keys), alternative = absolute, alt_flag = scale_flag) |>
    inner_join(base, by = pair_keys) |>
    filter(is.finite(base), is.finite(alternative)) |>
    mutate(change = alternative - base, comparison = name,
      scale_flag = base_flag | alt_flag)
}
comparisons <- function(data) {
  bind_rows(
    pair_models(data, "Lognormal", "Both PLD", "Both PLD"),
    pair_models(data, "Lognormal", "Survey PLD", "Survey PLD"),
    pair_models(data, "Lognormal", "Catch PLD", "Catch PLD"),
    pair_models(data, "No occurrence", "Fixed detection", "Occurrence added")
  )
}
pulse_pairs <- comparisons(pulse_metrics)
older_pairs <- comparisons(older)
prescribed_pairs <- if (nrow(pulse_metrics)) {
  prescribed_m <- filter(pulse_metrics, design == "sampling", metric == "M pulse height") |>
    mutate(truth = 0.35, signed = est - truth, absolute = abs(signed))
  comparisons(prescribed_m)
} else data.frame()
paired_mean <- function(x) if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_
paired_ci <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) < 2L) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  mean(x) + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, length(x) - 1L) * sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
}
pair_summary <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(design, scenario, resolution, metric, comparison) |>
    summarise(pairs = n(), unflagged = sum(!scale_flag),
      baseline_error = mean(base), alternative_error = mean(alternative),
      lower = paired_ci(change)[1L], upper = paired_ci(change)[2L],
      unflagged_change = paired_mean(change[!scale_flag]), difference = mean(change),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(evidence = if_else(pairs < 12L, "Descriptive, fewer than 12 pairs", "At least 12 pairs"),
      effort = scenario_label(scenario))
}
pair_sentence <- function(d, target, label, unit) {
  if (!nrow(d)) return("")
  s <- filter(pair_summary(d), scenario == "standard", metric == target,
    comparison == label, resolution == 14L)
  if (!nrow(s)) return("")
  sprintf("For %d common numerical %s pairs at standard effort (%d within the tenfold SSB scale check), mean absolute %s was %.3f versus %.3f%s.%s",
    s$pairs, if (label == "Occurrence added") "ablation" else "lognormal/PLD",
    s$unflagged, if (target == "M pulse height") "M pulse-height error" else "age-14+ log-abundance error",
    s$baseline_error, s$alternative_error, unit,
    if (s$pairs < 12L) " This comparison is descriptive." else "")
}
m_sentence <- pair_sentence(pulse_pairs, "M pulse height", "Both PLD", " per year")
n_sentence <- pair_sentence(older_pairs, "Ages 14+", "Both PLD", "")
ablation_sentence <- pair_sentence(pulse_pairs, "M pulse height", "Occurrence added", " per year")
ablation_abundance <- pair_sentence(older_pairs, "Ages 14+", "Occurrence added", "")

read_primary_result <- function(d, target, label) {
  if (!nrow(d)) return(data.frame())
  filter(pair_summary(d), scenario == "standard", metric == target,
    comparison == label, resolution == 14L)
}
evidence_sentence <- function(d, target, quantity) {
  s <- read_primary_result(d, target, "Both PLD")
  if (!nrow(s)) {
    wording <- if (study_complete) {
      "No common successful fits supported the %s comparison."
    } else {
      "The %s comparison awaits common successful fits."
    }
    return(sprintf(wording, quantity))
  }
  if (s$pairs < 12L) {
    return(sprintf("The %s comparison has too few common numerical pairs for a firm conclusion.", quantity))
  }
  if (s$upper < 0) {
    out <- sprintf("At standard effort, both-stream PLD reduced %s error on the common numerical pairs.", quantity)
  } else if (s$lower > 0) {
    out <- sprintf("At standard effort, both-stream PLD increased %s error on the common numerical pairs.", quantity)
  } else {
    out <- sprintf("At standard effort, the paired interval for %s included no change in error.", quantity)
  }
  if (is.finite(s$unflagged_change) && sign(s$unflagged_change) != sign(s$difference)) {
    out <- paste(out, "The mean change reversed direction in the unflagged pairs.")
  }
  out
}
m_evidence <- evidence_sentence(pulse_pairs, "M pulse height", "M pulse-height")
n_evidence <- evidence_sentence(older_pairs, "Ages 14+", "age-14+ abundance")
primary_evidence <- if (nzchar(m_sentence) || nzchar(n_sentence)) {
  paste(m_evidence, n_evidence)
} else if (study_complete) {
  "No common successful fits supported either primary comparison."
} else {
  "The mortality and older-fish comparisons await common successful fits."
}
abstract_results <- paste(Filter(nzchar, c(m_sentence, n_sentence, ablation_sentence,
  primary_evidence)), collapse = " ")

plot_paired <- function(d, axis_label) {
  pair_summary(d) |>
    ggplot(aes(difference, comparison, shape = evidence, size = pairs)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), orientation = "y",
      width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.45, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(colour = "#126782") +
    facet_grid(metric ~ effort, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Descriptive, fewer than 12 pairs" = 1, "At least 12 pairs" = 16)) +
    labs(x = axis_label, y = NULL, size = "Paired histories", shape = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## Abstract

At low abundance a survey or catch sample can record zero even though fish
remain in the stock. Excluding these records can discard evidence that
older fish have become scarce. We asked whether retaining zeros improved
estimates of older cod and a late increase in natural mortality. We
simulated 30 years of fishing and survey monitoring inspired by Northern
cod, with fishing declining before natural mortality rose. We fitted the
same observations with the positive-only lognormal and a Poisson-link
delta lognormal (PLD) that uses zeros and positives. A fixed-detection
comparison isolated the information in recording fish or recording zero
while holding the positive likelihood fixed. This report includes
`r length(sampling)` of 24 planned SimSurvey histories and
`r n_controlled` controlled `r ngettext(n_controlled, "history", "histories")`.
Of the `r attempted_main` checkpointed
SimSurvey fits, `r passed_main` passed numerical checks. `r abstract_results`

## How the experiment isolates the effect of zeros

For a predicted arithmetic mean \(\widetilde Y\) and half-detection level
\(\widetilde Y_{50}\), PLD assigns probability of zero

\[
p_0 = 2^{-\widetilde Y/\widetilde Y_{50}} .
\]

The corresponding lognormal mean on the log scale among positive records
is \(\log\{\widetilde Y/(1-p_0)\}-\sigma^2/2\), where \(\sigma\) is the
observation log-SD. The ordinary lognormal fits positive records and uses
\(\log(\widetilde Y)\) on that scale. Switching between these families
changes both the treatment of zeros and the positive likelihood. A separate
comparison fixes the two half-detection levels from independent calibration
histories and removes the Bernoulli contributions for zeros and positives
from one fit. Both fits keep the same positive density. The exact PLD
control fixes those levels at their true values and repeats the comparison.
[Thorson (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266)

The SimSurvey design has no single true half-detection level. Its
calibration relates recorded zeros to the simulated whole-area survey
index and realized removals, using six independent histories at standard
effort. These histories supply no recovery measures. The controlled
likelihood tests use exact PLD draws and multinomial age samples, which
introduce varying sample size and dependence through a shared sample
total. Fit comparisons use the same observations and starting rules
within each history. We estimate a normal-shaped age pattern and a separate
annual scale for F, an age-shared AR(1) process for M, a recruitment random
walk and exact cohort transitions. The survey catchability curve is logistic
in age. Cohort initialization uses exponential survival in the assessment.
The calibration plots use fitted data. The stock recovery comparisons use
known simulation truth.

The standard-effort SimSurvey fits include lognormal, survey-only PLD,
catch-only PLD, PLD for both, and the fixed-detection pair. Low and high
effort compare lognormal with PLD for both. The run has checkpointed
`r attempted_main` of `r planned_main` planned fits and `r failed_inputs`
failed input histories. `r if (study_complete) "All planned histories have been attempted." else "The run is in progress."`

```{r fixed-detection, results='asis'}
calibrated <- filter(fit_status, design == "sampling", scenario == "standard",
  model == "Fixed detection")
values <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(fits[calibrated$attempt], function(r) {
  r$value$calibration
}))
if (length(values)) {
  y50 <- values[[1L]]
  stopifnot(all(vapply(values, identical, logical(1), y50)))
  cat(sprintf("The independent calibration fixed the Gillnet and RV half-detection levels at %.3g and %.3g thousand fish.",
    y50[["catch"]], y50[["index"]]))
}
```

## What F and M did the simulator generate?

Fully selected F was 0.06 per year through year 4, increased to 0.22 by
year 8, stayed there through year 10, then fell to 0.06 by year 13 and to
0.035 by year 20. Natural mortality M remained 0.25 through year 13,
increased to 0.60 by year 16, stayed there through year 19, then fell to
0.40 by year 24. Both late rates held through year 30. Rates were
interpolated between those years. The survey
sampled the population at the start of each year. Fish lost to mortality
that year affect later cohorts and survey observations.

The cohort calculation uses the prescribed total mortality \(Z=F+M\).
SimSurvey allocates catches across the fishing grounds under this
mortality budget. A fishery that meets its total target can still have a
different catch-at-age pattern. The realized \(F\) is calculated from
allocated catch at age using the Baranov equation, and realized \(M\)
is the difference between prescribed \(Z\) and realized \(F\).
[SimSurvey methods](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0232822)
[Pinned fishery implementation](https://github.com/PaulRegular/SimSurvey/blob/29a1b03350c274f88dac108fb95f9446eac79233/R/fishery_engine.R)

```{r mortality, fig.cap="Prescribed and realized mortality averaged over ages 5–10 using the same simulated abundance weights. Thin lines represent individual histories. Thicker lines show medians. Grey bands mark the early fishing peak and the later natural mortality plateau."}
reference <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(x) mutate(x$reference, history = x$id)))
audit <- data.frame()
if (nrow(reference)) {
  audit <- reference |>
    filter(age %in% 5:10, is.finite(F_realized), is.finite(M_realized), N > 0) |>
    group_by(history, year) |>
    summarise(F_prescribed = weighted.mean(F_reference, N),
      F_realized = weighted.mean(F_realized, N),
      M_prescribed = weighted.mean(M_reference, N),
      M_realized = weighted.mean(M_realized, N),
      Z_prescribed = weighted.mean(Z, N), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(Z_realized = F_realized + M_realized)
  rates <- tidyr::pivot_longer(audit, -c(history, year), names_to = c("rate", "source"),
    names_sep = "_", values_to = "value")
  medians <- rates |>
    group_by(year, rate, source) |>
    summarise(value = median(value), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(rates, aes(year, value, colour = source, linetype = source)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 8, xmax = 10, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = .09) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 16, xmax = 19, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = .09) +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(history, source)), alpha = .22) +
    geom_line(data = medians, linewidth = .9) +
    facet_wrap(~rate, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(prescribed = "#353535", realized = "#126782")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(prescribed = "dashed", realized = "solid")) +
    labs(x = "Simulation year", y = "Abundance-weighted rate (per year)",
      colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
}
```

## How often did monitoring report zeros?

The Gillnet program monitored 25%, 50%, or 100% of the same realized
fishing operations, with up to 150 fish aged per sampled operation.
The RV survey sampled one, two, or four tows per 1,000 square kilometres,
with at least two per stratum. Tow swept area was 0.0018 square kilometres.
The stratified estimate expands catches by swept area to preserve the
whole-area index target. Fewer encounters can still change the frequency
of zeros and the support for estimating age composition. Gillnet age-at-catch
estimates require monitoring support. Unsampled or unsupported records
remain missing.

```{r zeros, fig.cap="Zero frequency at the age resolution of the Northern cod example. Only sampled rows with either a zero or positive value enter the denominator. The final tick pools ages 14–20. The dashed line shows Northern cod."}
zero_rows <- data.frame()
if (length(sampling)) {
  zero_rows <- bind_rows(pld_cod_observation_rows(cod_obs),
    filter(pld_sim_observation_rows(sampling), age >= 2L)) |>
    mutate(program = recode(component, catch = "Commercial catch", index = "RV index"),
      effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Northern cod", "low", "standard", "high"),
        labels = c("Northern cod", "Low", "Standard", "High")))
  zero_rows |>
    group_by(program, effort, age) |>
    summarise(frequency = mean(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    ggplot(aes(age, frequency, colour = effort, linetype = effort)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .7) + geom_point(size = 1.3) + facet_wrap(~program) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2, 14, 2), labels = c(seq(2, 12, 2), "14+")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Northern cod" = "#353535", Low = "#C44C27",
      Standard = "#126782", High = "#258375")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Northern cod" = "dashed", Low = "solid",
      Standard = "solid", High = "solid")) +
    labs(x = "Modeled age", y = "Observed zero frequency", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r zero-support, results='asis'}
if (nrow(zero_rows)) {
  support <- bind_rows(mutate(zero_rows, ages = "2–14+"),
    mutate(filter(zero_rows, age >= 10L), ages = "10–14+")) |>
    group_by(program, effort, ages) |>
    summarise(zeros = sum(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      sampled = sum(is.finite(obs)), missing = sum(is.na(obs)),
      rate = scales::percent(zeros / sampled, accuracy = 0.1), .groups = "drop")
  print(knitr::kable(support, col.names = c("Program", "Effort", "Ages",
    "Zeros", "Sampled", "Missing", "Zero rate")))
}
```

Northern cod's unsurveyed years contribute no zeros. The Northern cod
comparison gives an empirical reference for the frequency of zeros. A
similar fraction can arise from different age and year patterns.

### When and at what ages did zeros occur?

For SimSurvey, years 1–4 precede the fishing increase, years 5–13 cover the
fishing increase and decline, years 14–23 cover the rise and decline in
natural mortality, and years 24–30 are the late period. The Northern cod
panels use observed calendar periods. Their timing describes the data
available for the example and does not assign a cause to historical zeros.

```{r zeros-by-phase, fig.width=9, fig.height=7.8, fig.cap="Fraction of sampled age-year cells recorded as zero by phase or calendar period. Each tile has its own denominator. Grey marks cells with no sampled observations. Age 14+ pools native ages 14–20."}
phase_support <- data.frame()
if (nrow(zero_rows)) {
  phase_support <- zero_rows |>
    mutate(period = case_when(
      effort == "Northern cod" & year <= 1991L ~ "1983–91",
      effort == "Northern cod" & year <= 1997L ~ "1992–97",
      effort == "Northern cod" & year <= 2015L ~ "1998–2015",
      effort == "Northern cod" ~ "2016–25",
      year <= 4L ~ "1–4",
      year <= 13L ~ "5–13",
      year <= 23L ~ "14–23",
      TRUE ~ "24–30"
    ),
    period = factor(period, levels = c("1983–91", "1992–97", "1998–2015", "2016–25",
      "1–4", "5–13", "14–23", "24–30"))) |>
    group_by(effort, program, period, age) |>
    summarise(zeros = sum(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE), sampled = sum(is.finite(obs)),
      missing = sum(is.na(obs)), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(frequency = if_else(sampled > 0L, zeros / sampled, NA_real_))
  ggplot(phase_support, aes(period, age, fill = frequency)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .23) +
    facet_wrap(vars(effort, program), ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 6, 10, 14), labels = c("2", "6", "10", "14+")) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1),
      labels = scales::label_percent(), na.value = "#C6C9CB") +
    labs(x = "Calendar period or simulation years", y = "Modeled age", fill = "Zero frequency") +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r phase-support, results='asis'}
if (nrow(phase_support)) {
  denominator <- filter(phase_support, age == 14L) |>
    transmute(program, effort, period, zeros, sampled, missing)
  print(knitr::kable(denominator,
    col.names = c("Program", "Effort", "Period", "Zeros", "Sampled", "Missing"),
    caption = "Age-14+ observation counts underlying the last row of each panel."))
}
```


### What does the 14+ group represent?

The simulated population has a separate abundance at ages 14 through 20.
The fitted assessment combines those ages into one group. The true 14+
abundance is their sum at the beginning of each year. Fish surviving the
oldest native age leave the operating population. In the assessment, terminal
survivors remain in the plus group. The distinction can matter when older
fish accumulate. The fitted 14+ mortality and catchability also apply
across ages whose native selectivities differ.

```{r pooled-zeros, results='asis'}
if (length(sampling)) {
  cod_tail <- bind_rows(lapply(c("catch", "index"), function(component) {
    cod_obs[[component]] |>
      filter(year %in% 1983:2025, age %in% 14:20) |>
      transmute(year, age, obs, component = component, history = NA_integer_,
        effort = "Northern cod")
  }))
  simulated_tail <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(h) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(h$series), function(e) {
      raw <- h$series[[e]]$observations
      bind_rows(transmute(raw$native_catch, year, age, obs, component = "catch"),
        transmute(raw$native_index, year, age, obs, component = "index")) |>
        filter(age %in% 14:20) |>
        mutate(history = h$id, effort = e)
    }))
  }))
  pool_summary <- bind_rows(cod_tail, simulated_tail) |>
    group_by(component, effort, history, year) |>
    summarise(complete = n_distinct(age) == 7L && all(is.finite(obs)),
      positive = complete && sum(obs) > 0,
      n_zero = sum(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(component, effort) |>
    summarise(native_zeros = sum(n_zero[complete]), absorbed = sum(n_zero[positive]),
      positive_with_zeros = sum(positive & n_zero > 0), complete_14plus = sum(complete),
      incomplete_14plus = sum(!complete), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(absorbed_share = if_else(native_zeros > 0L,
      scales::percent(absorbed / native_zeros, accuracy = 0.1), NA_character_),
      program = recode(component, catch = "Commercial catch", index = "RV index"),
      effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Northern cod", "low", "standard", "high"),
        labels = c("Northern cod", "Low", "Standard", "High"))) |>
    arrange(program, effort) |>
    select(program, effort, native_zeros, absorbed, absorbed_share, positive_with_zeros,
      complete_14plus, incomplete_14plus)
  print(knitr::kable(pool_summary, col.names = c("Program", "Effort",
    "Native zeros", "Zeros in positive pools", "Share absorbed", "Positive pools with zeros",
    "Complete 14+ pools", "Incomplete 14+ pools"),
    caption = "Native ages 14–20 can contribute zeros to an observed 14+ total that is positive. The zero share uses only complete age sets."))
}
```

```{r plus-audit, fig.cap="Effective age-14+ selectivity and catchability as a percentage of their age-14 values. Thin lines show individual histories. At the prescribed Z, the effective catch selectivity reproduces total reference catch across ages 14–20. The RV calculation weights catchability by beginning-of-year abundance."}
if (nrow(reference)) {
  terminal <- reference |>
    filter(age >= 14L, N > 0) |>
    mutate(exposure = N * (-expm1(-Z)) / Z, q = pld_q(age)) |>
    group_by(history, year) |>
    filter(any(age == 14L)) |>
    summarise(Gillnet = weighted.mean(selectivity, exposure) / selectivity[age == 14L],
      RV = weighted.mean(q, N) / q[age == 14L], .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Gillnet, RV), names_to = "program", values_to = "ratio")
  ggplot(terminal, aes(year, 100 * ratio, group = history)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_line(alpha = .45, colour = "#126782") +
    facet_wrap(~program, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Simulation year", y = "Effective value (% of age 14)")
}
```

```{r omitted-survivors, results='asis'}
if (length(sampling)) {
  oldest <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling, function(h) mutate(h$oldest, history = h$id)))
  omitted <- oldest |>
    inner_join(reference |>
      filter(age >= 14L) |>
      group_by(history, year) |>
      summarise(tail = sum(N), .groups = "drop"),
      by = c("history", "year")) |>
    mutate(relative_to_tail = if_else(tail > 0, survivor / tail, NA_real_))
  cat(sprintf(paste("Up to %s individual fish survived the oldest simulated age in a year.",
      "These omissions amounted to at most %.2f%% of total beginning-of-year abundance",
      "or %.2f%% of beginning-of-year abundance at ages 14–20."),
    format(round(max(oldest$survivor, na.rm = TRUE)), big.mark = ","),
    100 * max(oldest$proportion, na.rm = TRUE),
    100 * max(omitted$relative_to_tail, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

## Which models could be compared?

Numerical success requires passing tinyAM's numerical checks. Frequency of
success and recovery on successful pairs answer different questions.
The table includes attempts where PLD could not estimate its half-detection
scale. A program with zero recorded nondetections gives insufficient support
to estimate the scale freely. Paired results therefore describe the
particular histories for which both fits could be evaluated.

```{r fit-counts, results='asis'}
if (nrow(fit_status)) {
  counts <- fit_status |>
    left_join(select(scale, all_of(keys), scale_flag), by = keys) |>
    group_by(scenario, resolution, model) |>
    summarise(attempted = n(), passed = sum(success),
      scale_flagged = sum(scale_flag, na.rm = TRUE),
      no_zeros = sum(grepl("no eligible sampled zeros", error, ignore.case = TRUE)),
      other_errors = sum(nzchar(error) & !grepl("no eligible sampled zeros", error, ignore.case = TRUE)),
      warnings = sum(warnings > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scenario = scenario_label(scenario), model = factor(model, levels = arms)) |>
    arrange(scenario, resolution, model)
  print(knitr::kable(counts, col.names = c("Design or effort", "Terminal age",
    "Model", "Attempted", "Passed", "SSB flag", "No zeros", "Other errors", "Warned")))
} else {
  cat("This copy has no fit checkpoints.")
}
```

```{r failed-checks, results='asis'}
sampling_fits <- filter(fit_status, design == "sampling", !success)
numerical_failures <- bind_rows(lapply(sampling_fits$attempt, function(attempt) {
  checks <- fits[[attempt]]$value$numerical
  if (is.data.frame(checks)) {
    transmute(filter(checks, status == "fail"), attempt = attempt, check)
  }
}))
if (nrow(numerical_failures)) {
  failures <- count(numerical_failures, check, sort = TRUE)
  reasons <- paste0(failures$check, " (", failures$n, ")")
  cat(sprintf(paste("%d SimSurvey fits failed at least one numerical check.",
      "The checks that failed were %s. A fit can fail more than one check.\n\n"),
    n_distinct(numerical_failures$attempt), paste(reasons, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

Some numerical passes can estimate an extreme stock size. For small F,
catch is roughly proportional to \(NF\), and the survey index is proportional
to \(Nq\). Increasing abundance and reducing fishing mortality and
catchability can then leave the observations nearly unchanged. A fit is
flagged here if its median SSB ratio is outside 0.1–10. The flag uses
simulation truth. All numerical passes remain in the primary comparisons,
and the sensitivity uses pairs where neither fit is flagged.

```{r scale-check, fig.cap="Median annual fitted SSB divided by true SSB for each numerically successful SimSurvey fit. The shaded band spans one tenth to ten times the true value. It illustrates extreme scale errors and does not define acceptable biological agreement."}
if (nrow(scale)) {
  d <- filter(scale, design == "sampling", resolution == 14L,
    is.finite(ssb_ratio), ssb_ratio > 0)
  if (nrow(d)) {
    ggplot(d, aes(factor(model, levels = arms), ssb_ratio)) +
      annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0.1, ymax = 10, alpha = .12) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
      geom_jitter(width = .13, alpha = .55, colour = "#126782") +
      scale_y_log10() + facet_wrap(~scenario_label(scenario)) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Fitted SSB / true SSB") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  }
}
```

## Did PLD recover the later M pulse?

The main mortality measure is mean M in years 16–19 minus mean M in
years 1–10. We report its signed error and compare absolute error on
matched histories. Early F is the mean in years 8–10 minus the mean in
years 1–4. Late F and M are annual means over years 24–30. Annual F and M
comparisons use ages 5–10, with the same true abundance weights in the
fitted and reference summaries. The SimSurvey recovery target is the
rate realized by the simulator. We also compare pulse-height errors
against the prescribed M increase of 0.350 per year.

```{r fitted-mortality, fig.cap="Fishing and natural mortality at standard effort on histories where both families passed. Thin curves show fitted histories and thick curves show their median. Dashed lines show the median realized rate on those same histories. Both fitted and realized rates use identical true abundance weights over ages 5–10."}
if (nrow(annual)) {
  d <- filter(annual, design == "sampling", scenario == "standard", resolution == 14L,
    quantity %in% c("F_bar", "M_bar"), model %in% c("Lognormal", "Both PLD")) |>
    group_by(history, quantity, year) |>
    filter(n_distinct(model) == 2L) |>
    ungroup()
  if (nrow(d)) {
    d <- mutate(d, quantity = recode(quantity, F_bar = "Fishing mortality (F)",
      M_bar = "Natural mortality (M)"))
    truth <- distinct(d, quantity, history, year, truth) |>
      group_by(quantity, year) |>
      summarise(truth = median(truth), .groups = "drop")
    medians <- d |>
      group_by(quantity, model, year) |>
      summarise(est = median(est), .groups = "drop")
    ggplot(d, aes(year, est, colour = model)) +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 8, xmax = 10, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = .09) +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 16, xmax = 19, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = .09) +
      geom_line(aes(group = interaction(model, history)), alpha = .2) +
      geom_line(data = medians, linewidth = .9) +
      geom_line(data = truth, aes(year, truth), inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = 2) +
      facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y") + scale_colour_manual(values = arm_palette) +
      labs(x = "Simulation year", y = "Abundance-weighted rate (per year)", colour = NULL) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  }
}
```

```{r pulse-signed, fig.cap="Signed error of the late natural mortality pulse and early fishing mortality increase. Positive values mean the fitted increase exceeded the realized increase. Each point represents a numerically successful fit."}
if (nrow(pulse_metrics)) {
  d <- filter(pulse_metrics, design == "sampling", resolution == 14L,
    metric %in% c("M pulse height", "Early F increase"))
  if (nrow(d)) {
    ggplot(d, aes(signed, factor(model, levels = rev(arms)))) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
      geom_jitter(height = .14, width = 0, colour = "#126782", alpha = .55) +
      facet_grid(metric ~ scenario_label(scenario), scales = "free_x") +
      labs(x = "Estimated minus realized increase (per year)", y = NULL)
  }
}
```

```{r pulse-paired, fig.cap="Paired changes in absolute error for the M pulse, early F and late rates. Negative values favour PLD or the fit including occurrence. Bars mark approximate 95% Monte Carlo intervals from independent histories. Open circles show descriptive comparisons with fewer than 12 common pairs."}
if (nrow(pulse_pairs)) {
  d <- filter(pulse_pairs, resolution == 14L)
  if (nrow(d)) plot_paired(d, "Change in absolute error (per year)")
}
```

```{r primary-denominator, results='asis'}
primary_comparison <- function(d, metric_name) {
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  pair_summary(d) |>
    filter(metric == metric_name, resolution == 14L, design == "sampling",
      comparison %in% c("Both PLD", "Occurrence added"))
}
primary <- bind_rows(primary_comparison(pulse_pairs, "M pulse height"),
  primary_comparison(older_pairs, "Ages 14+"))
if (nrow(primary)) {
  primary |>
    select(metric, effort, comparison, pairs, unflagged, baseline_error,
      alternative_error, difference, unflagged_change) |>
    arrange(metric, effort, comparison) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Quantity", "Effort", "Comparison",
      "Numerical pairs", "Unflagged pairs", "Baseline error", "Alternative error",
      "Paired change", "Change among unflagged")) |>
    print()
} else {
  cat("No successful pairs are available yet for the primary comparisons.")
}
```

For Both PLD the baseline is lognormal. For Occurrence added the baseline
uses the same positive density and fixed detection levels with the reporting
indicator removed. Reported absolute errors average over paired histories.
Pairs with fewer than 12 histories are descriptive.

```{r prescribed-sensitivity, results='asis'}
if (nrow(prescribed_pairs)) {
  realized <- filter(pulse_pairs, design == "sampling", metric == "M pulse height",
    comparison == "Both PLD", resolution == 14L)
  prescribed <- filter(prescribed_pairs, comparison == "Both PLD", resolution == 14L)
  sensitivity <- inner_join(
    select(realized, history, scenario, realized = change),
    select(prescribed, history, scenario, prescribed = change),
    by = c("history", "scenario"))
  if (nrow(sensitivity)) {
    check <- group_by(sensitivity, scenario) |>
      summarise(pairs = n(), realized = mean(realized), prescribed = mean(prescribed),
        .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(effort = scenario_label(scenario))
    print(knitr::kable(select(check, effort, pairs, realized, prescribed), digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Effort", "Numerical pairs", "Realized M benchmark", "Prescribed M benchmark"),
      caption = "Paired change in absolute pulse error (per year), both PLD minus lognormal."))
  }
}
```

## Did PLD recover older fish during and after the pulse?

The primary abundance measure uses ages 14+ in years 16–23. We compare the
reported fitted abundance directly with the sum of true ages 14–20, in
thousands of fish. At less aggregated ages we compare the sum over
ages 10–13 on the same years. For each history, signed log error averages
\(\log(\widehat N/N)\) and measures bias. Mean absolute log error averages
its magnitude before comparing models. Positive signed error means
overestimation, and a difference of \(\log(2)\) represents a twofold error.

```{r older-trajectories, fig.cap="Age-14+ abundance at each effort, on the histories where lognormal and both-PLD fits passed numerical checks. Thin curves show individual fitted histories. Lines and dashed truth show medians over the same paired histories. The shaded years are used in the primary abundance comparison."}
if (nrow(age_abundance)) {
  d <- filter(age_abundance, design == "sampling", resolution == 14L, age == 14L,
    model %in% c("Lognormal", "Both PLD")) |>
    group_by(scenario, history, year) |>
    filter(n_distinct(model) == 2L) |>
    ungroup()
  if (nrow(d)) {
    truth <- distinct(d, scenario, history, year, truth) |>
      group_by(scenario, year) |>
      summarise(truth = median(truth), .groups = "drop")
    medians <- d |>
      group_by(scenario, model, year) |>
      summarise(est = median(est), .groups = "drop")
    ggplot(d, aes(year, est, colour = model)) +
      annotate("rect", xmin = 16, xmax = 23, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = .1) +
      geom_line(aes(group = interaction(model, history)), alpha = .22) +
      geom_line(data = medians, linewidth = .9) +
      geom_line(data = truth, aes(year, truth), inherit.aes = FALSE,
        linetype = 2, linewidth = .8) +
      facet_wrap(~scenario_label(scenario)) + scale_y_log10() +
      scale_colour_manual(values = arm_palette) +
      labs(x = "Simulation year", y = "Abundance at ages 14+ (thousand fish)",
        colour = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  }
}
```

```{r older-signed, fig.cap="Signed log bias for older fish over years 16–23. A point is one successful fit. Positive values indicate overestimation. Open points flag median SSB ratios outside the tenfold range."}
if (nrow(older)) {
  d <- filter(older, design == "sampling") |>
    left_join(select(scale, all_of(keys), scale_flag), by = keys)
  if (nrow(d)) {
    ggplot(d, aes(signed, factor(model, levels = rev(arms)), shape = scale_flag)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
      geom_jitter(height = .13, width = 0, alpha = .65, colour = "#126782") +
      facet_grid(metric ~ scenario_label(scenario), scales = "free_x") +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 1, "FALSE" = 16),
        labels = c("FALSE" = "Within tenfold", "TRUE" = "SSB flagged")) +

      theme(legend.position = "bottom")

}

```{r older-paired, fig.cap="Paired changes in mean absolute log error for the same older ages and years. Negative values mean the indicated PLD approach was closer to the true abundance."}
if (nrow(older_pairs)) plot_paired(older_pairs, "Change in mean absolute log-abundance error")
```

if (nrow(annual)) {

```{r interval-support, fig.cap="Coverage of nominal 95% intervals for annual SSB, recruitment and M at standard effort, evaluated on common years and histories with finite intervals from both fits. The size of a point shows the number of paired histories. Intervals for the true-abundance-weighted F summary and older-age abundance are unavailable."}
if (nrow(annual)) {

## Did the fitted observation model describe the zeros and positives?

Zero-probability calibration compares the observed fraction of zeros
against the average fitted probability among the same observations.
The amount comparison uses the arithmetic mean of observed positive
records versus the average fitted mean conditional on a positive. Both
are in-sample diagnostics.

```{r calibration, fig.cap="Calibration of fitted zero probability in successful joint PLD fits. Each point summarizes supported age-year rows in one fitted probability bin. Number of rows determines point size. The diagonal marks agreement."}
obs <- bind_rows(lapply(which(fit_status$success & fit_status$model == "Both PLD" &
  fit_status$resolution == 14L), function(i) {
    row <- fit_status[i, ]
    bind_rows(fits[[row$attempt]]$value$obs, .id = "component") |>
      mutate(design = row$design, scenario = row$scenario)
  }))
if (nrow(obs) && "p_zero" %in% names(obs)) {
  calibration <- obs |>
    filter(family == "pld_lognormal", is.finite(obs), is.finite(p_zero)) |>
    mutate(bin = cut(p_zero, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
    group_by(component, scenario, bin) |>
    summarise(predicted = mean(p_zero), observed = mean(obs == 0), rows = n(), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(calibration)) {
    ggplot(calibration, aes(predicted, observed, size = rows)) +
      geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
      geom_point(colour = "#126782", alpha = .75) +
      facet_grid(component ~ scenario_label(scenario)) +
      coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
      labs(x = "Fitted zero probability", y = "Observed zero frequency", size = "Rows")
  }
}
```

```{r positive-amounts, fig.cap="Mean observed and fitted amounts for positive records in standard-effort joint PLD fits. Each point uses the same rows within a fitted-mean group. The diagonal marks agreement. Axes are logarithmic and values are in thousands of fish."}
if (nrow(obs) && all(c("log_pred_positive", "sd") %in% names(obs))) {
  amount <- obs |>
    filter(scenario == "standard", family == "pld_lognormal", is.finite(obs), obs > 0) |>
    mutate(positive_mean = exp(log_pred_positive + sd^2 / 2)) |>
    filter(is.finite(positive_mean), positive_mean > 0) |>
    group_by(component) |>
    mutate(bin = ntile(positive_mean, 8L)) |>
    group_by(component, bin) |>
    summarise(predicted = mean(positive_mean), observed = mean(obs), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(amount)) {
    ggplot(amount, aes(predicted, observed)) +
      geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
      geom_point(colour = "#126782") + facet_wrap(~component, scales = "free") +
      scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
      labs(x = "Fitted positive mean (thousand fish)", y = "Observed positive mean (thousand fish)")
  }
}
```

## What does this imply for assessments?

`r m_evidence` `r n_evidence` `r ablation_abundance`

The comparison of lognormal and full PLD measures the net effect of changing
the observation family. The fixed-detection comparison answers the narrower
question of how much the record of zeros and positives adds after the
positive density is held fixed. Small paired samples, extreme stock-scale
estimates, and changes between the full and unflagged sets qualify either
result. Sampled zeros can inform low catchability-weighted abundance.
The interpretation of losses as fishing or natural mortality still depends
on the catch data and population assumptions.

The study simulated an early F peak and a later M increase. It measures
recovery for that ordering and the monitoring designs above. It provides
no estimate of false pulse detections under constant mortality or of
forecast skill. A fixed detection scale within a stream may be inadequate
when effort or sampling methods vary through a time series.

Seeds, source revisions, observation support and every attempted fit are
recorded with the study checkpoints.
